subject: Bridge credit smoothing & step-down option for renewal
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana@brightwell.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Bridge credit smoothing & step-down option for renewal

Hi Dana —

Thanks again for a productive demo last week. Based on the usage pattern you shared and the Q3 budget window, I wanted to propose a renewal structure that smooths Brightwell’s spend over the first 18 months while keeping unit economics predictable for Redwood. Attached is a small pricing workbook (redwood-pricing-options-2028q2.xlsx).

High level proposal (flexible, can adjust):
- Term: 24 months (Apr 1, 2028 — Mar 31, 2030)
- Year 1 commit: 9M tokens/month average (tiered pricing)
- Year 2 commit: 6M tokens/month average (step-down to match forecasted usage)
- Bridge credit: $250,000 applied in Year 1 and amortized across Q2–Q4 invoices to ease cash impact
- Auto-renew: 12-month notice opt-out; if no notice, renews at Year 2 rates with CPI adjustment capped at 5%
- Co-terming: we can align start/end dates with your existing vendor calendar if helpful (need legal to confirm amendment wording)

Why this helps Brightwell: immediate effective unit-rate relief up-front via bridge credit, predictable annualized cap in Year 2, and a built-in escape if usage materially undershoots.

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm whether procurement should be looped in now (I’ve included a sample CC below).
2) If this looks directionally OK, I’ll loop in Karthik and Marissa to finalize the amortization approach and pricing bands, and ask legal to draft an amendment reflecting the step-down schedule.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call this week if you want to walk through the workbook.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood-pricing-options-2028q2.xlsx
From: Dana Liu <dana@brightwell.io>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@brightwell.io>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bridge credit smoothing & step-down option for renewal

Camila —

Appreciate the fast follow. A few quick clarifying questions from our side: 
- Can the bridge credit be paid as a credit on invoices rather than an up-front check? That would be easier for our finance team.
- Year 2 step-down looks reasonable, but can we add a true-up clause if quarterly actuals exceed the committed baseline by >25%? We want to avoid surprise overages.
- Auto-renew notice: 12 months is a long runway for us; can we do 90 days notice instead?

I’ve CC’d procurement so they can flag any contract timing constraints. They’ll likely want the amendment and SOW in PDF form for their vendor intake.

Regards,
Dana Liu
Head of Platform Engineering | Brightwell Health
dana@brightwell.io

Attachment: Brightwell_forecast_Q2Q3.xlsx

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana@brightwell.io>, Procurement Team <procure@brightwell.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bridge credit smoothing & step-down option for renewal

Dana / Brightwell procurement —

Thanks for the quick questions, Dana. Short answers below and next steps at the bottom.

- Bridge credit mechanics: yes, we can apply the $250k as invoice credits spread over Q2–Q4 invoices rather than an up-front payment. The attached draft SOW notes the amortization schedule.
- True-up clause: we can include a quarterly true-up if usage exceeds committed baseline by >25%; overage rates would follow the Year 1 tiered schedule until the next quarter true-up is applied. We can add a safety cap (e.g., no more than 50% above forecast without separate negotiation).
- Auto-renew notice: we can move to a 90-day opt-out notice instead of 12 months. To preserve predictability for both sides, we propose an alternative: 90-day notice but with a 4% CPI floor if renewal happens with less than 6 months’ notice. Open to other constructs if procurement prefers.

Internal context for Redwood team:
- I’ve attached the pricing workbook with two amortization options (linear across 3 quarters vs accelerated front-load). Please review which preserves margin while helping Brightwell cashflow.
- If legal will prepare an amendment, we should confirm co-terming language (Brightwell requested alignment) and whether we want an SLO credit incentive if latency/availability SLOs exceed targets in Year 1.

Proposed next steps:
1) Procurement confirms 90-day notice ok and whether they need a vendor intake PDF (we’ll provide Brightwell_SOW_v2.pdf).
2) Karthik / Marissa to confirm which amortization option we should present (linear vs front-load).
3) If approved, legal drafts amendment + SOW and we route DocuSign.

I’m available for a 20–30m sync this afternoon if helpful.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Brightwell_SOW_v2.pdf, redwood-pricing-options-2028q2.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bridge credit smoothing & step-down option for renewal (internal)

Team —

Quick internal note after reviewing Camila’s latest:
- Margin / concession framing: $250k bridge credit is OK if amortized across Q2–Q4 (linear). If Brightwell asks for accelerated front-load, we should limit to $150k to preserve deal-level margin.
- True-up: agree to quarterly true-ups at >25% over baseline; set an overage cap at 2x the standard per-token rate for any ad-hoc spikes to avoid gaming.
- Auto-renew: accept 90-day notice, but include a 4% CPI floor if notice <6 months as Camila suggested. That keeps renewal economics protected.
- SLO incentive: offer a 3% invoice credit if we exceed availability targets 99.95%+ for two consecutive quarters in Year 1 — good net-new value for Brightwell and limited downside for us.

Ask to Marissa: can you run final numbers on linear vs front-load amortization and confirm the blended unit rate impact on FY28 bookings? I’ll mark the deal green for legal to draft once we have that.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Sales Strategy | Redwood Inference
